engine: Scroll-scrubs an architect's camera move (a 3D fly-around / descent, 5-20s) frame by frame as you scroll — the Apple/AirPods technique. A pre-extracted numbered image sequence (ffmpeg) is preloaded and the right frame is painted to a <canvas> on scroll. NOT video.currentTime (which stutters: the source clip is ~1 keyframe per 192 frames, so every seek decodes the whole GOP). Zero decoder lag, locked 60fps, pixel-exact.

measured_teardown.move: the section PINS full-screen; scroll progress 0..1 maps to frame index 0..N-1 (a lerped/eased index so it glides instead of snapping); the canvas paints that frame. A preload gate holds (0..100) until preloadMin of frames is decoded, then reveals. Reversible.
measured_teardown.cited: Not a Springs/EVER teardown — a separate technique the user asked for (architect 3D fly-around clips, 5-20s, scrubbed smoothly). Reference: Apple product pages (AirPods/MacBook) scroll-driven canvas sequences. Source clip: nahirna arrival/descent 8s 24fps, 1 keyframe / 192 frames (proves currentTime is the wrong path).

frames.what: path prefix; a frame url = prefix + zero-padded(start+i) + ext.

count.what: number of frames in the sequence. 100-150 is plenty for a smooth scrub; more = heavier preload.

pad.what: zero-pad width of the frame number (f_001..f_120).

pinFactor.what: pin length = innerHeight*pinFactor. Longer = the clip scrubs over more scroll = slower, more cinematic.

lerp.what: frame-index smoothing on the ticker. Lower = glassier glide but more lag behind the scroll; higher = snappier, closer to the raw scroll.

preloadMin.what: fraction of frames decoded before the preload gate opens; the rest lazy-load. 0.5 = reveal at the halfway point.

cover.what: object-fit cover (fill the stage, crop) vs contain.

manageLenis.what: create+drive a Lenis (false if the page owns one).

entry: ScrollScrubVideo.init(target, opts) -> { trigger, lenis, paint, refresh, destroy }. Markup: .ssv-stage > canvas.ssv-canvas + [.ssv-preload (0..100 hint)] + [.ssv-content ...]. The engine preloads the sequence, paints frames to the canvas on scroll, and pins.
law: Lenis 1.1.13 -> gsap.ticker -> ScrollTrigger.update; lagSmoothing(0); the painted frame index is smoothed on the ticker (a PURE fn of the smoothed index); PIN full-screen (start 'top top', end '+=innerHeight*pinFactor', pin:true, pinSpacing:true, scrub:true); frames are decoded ONCE via createImageBitmap (NOT held as — a preloaded still holds compressed bytes so its first drawImage decodes inline and stutters; an ImageBitmap is a ready raster, drawImage is a cheap GPU copy); canvas drawImage only (no per-frame layout, no DOM churn); cap DPR (~1.25) so frames aren't upscaled and each paint stays cheap; NO mix-blend / NO backdrop over the canvas; NO WebGL (2d canvas); NEVER video.currentTime <-> scroll (decoder jank); reduced-motion/<=820px -> static (paint the last frame, no pin/scrub). owns_pin TRUE -> ONE scroll owner per page.
asset_pipeline: ffmpeg -i clip.mp4 -vf 'fps=15,scale=1280:720:flags=lanczos' -c:v libwebp -q:v 58 -compression_level 4 -method 4 frames/f_%03d.webp  (fps=15 over an 8s clip -> 120 frames; tune q for weight; ~30-60KB/frame target = 4-7MB/section). A 5s clip -> ~75 frames, a 20s clip -> sample to ~150.
gate_mode: the smoothness-gate's blank/pixel checks target /.media; this brick paints to a (no tag), so the gate reads 'blank 100%' falsely. Verify with a direct probe instead: the canvas is opaque (frames painted) every frame, the painted frame index advances 0->N-1 with scroll then reverses, fps>=50, jank<8%.
proven: lab: OUR nahirna arrival/descent fly-in (120 webp frames, 1280x720) — preload runs 0->100 then __LAB_OK__ (ssv-ready, NOT ssv-static); the section pins and the camera move scrubs frame-by-frame with scroll, gliding + reversible, the canvas opaque every frame. KEY FIX: first build held s and stuttered (13.8% long frames under 4x CPU throttle = decode-jank, each frame's first drawImage decoded the webp inline). Switched to createImageBitmap (decode once -> ready raster) + DPR cap 1.25: re-probed 0.2% long frames (2/953), 59.9fps, 0 empty-canvas frames. Smooth, no decoder jank. (Weight note: these dark night frames compressed to ~141KB ea = 17MB/120; tune -q:v / count / resolution per clip at integration — the engine is weight-independent.)
